title: kernel-v1 compatibility matrix evidence (v1)
description: Published compatibility matrix for kernel-v1 (Linux 5.15 / 6.1 / 6.6 / <current>) x (x86_64 / arm64) x (BTF / LSM / cgroup / TC / runtime) cells. The matrix is anchored by an explicit plan-pinned 'lock_kernel' so reviewers can prove no kernel has drifted silently between bench runs. The 'expected' table is the contract; 'actual' is what task 55 observed; per-cell entries explain the gap when they differ.

schema_version.description: Bumped on backward-incompatible shape changes. Currently always 1.

lock_kernel.description: Plan-pinned '<current>' kernel version string recorded at plan-lock time. Reviewers MUST verify the lock_kernel value matches the published plan; a mismatch implies a drift defect.

expected.description: 2D matrix keyed by [kernel_arch][cell_name] mapping to 'capable' | 'degraded' | 'blocked'. The expected value comes from the bench/schemas/compat-matrix.v1.json published table.

actual.description: 2D matrix keyed by [kernel_arch][cell_name] mapping to 'capable' | 'degraded' | 'blocked'. The actual value is what the privileged compatibility lane observed in task 55.

cells.description: Per-cell evaluation. Each entry joins the (kernel_arch, cell) tuple to its expected and actual status and the ok flag. Reviewers MUST verify every expected cell has a matching actual cell; missing cells fail the matrix.

pass_fail.description: True iff every cell in 'cells' has ok==true AND every expected cell is present in actual. False otherwise.

oneOf.description: Branch 1: pass_fail=true requires every cell to report ok=true. A cell that reports ok=false under pass_fail=true is the canonical mismatch.
Branch 2: pass_fail=false. The mismatch is on the producer side and is acceptable for review; this branch carries no further cell constraints.
